### Approach
`Cursor` materializes the input as `Array[Char]` (code points), so Unicode/surrogate content round-trips untouched and error positions are code-point indices. Two scanners (`parse_quoted_field`, `parse_unquoted_field`) feed `parse_record`; the top-level loop collapses `\r\n`, accepts lone `\r`, maps empty input to zero records, never adds a record for a trailing terminator, and enforces that every record matches the first record's field width. `print` quotes only fields containing `,`/`"`/`\n`/`\r`, doubles internal quotes, and terminates every record so `parse(print(doc)) == doc` for rectangular documents.

## What I built

A hand‑written, single‑pass state machine (no regex, no fixture lookup):

```
csv/
├── csv_spec.mbt          # frozen API (untouched)
├── csv.mbt               # @csv.parse / @csv.print façades
├── parser/
│   ├── moon.pkg
│   ├── parser.mbt        # scanner: records → fields
│   └── printer.mbt       # serializer (true inverse of the scanner)
├── csv_extra_test.mbt    # 36 added edge‑case tests
├── moon.pkg              # imports the parser subpackage
└── README.md             # architecture, algorithms, usage, testing
```

- **Scanner** (`parse_records` / `parse_record` / `parse_field`): walks the input by UTF‑16 code unit. `parse_unquoted_field` copies a run to the next `,`/terminator/EOF and rejects `"`; `parse_quoted_field` handles `""` escapes and embedded `,`/LF/CR/CRLF verbatim, then validates that only `,`/terminator/EOF follows the closing quote. LF, CRLF (one terminator), and lone CR are all accepted; empty input → zero records; a trailing terminator opens no extra record; every record must match the first record's field count. All malformed cases (unterminated quote incl. multi‑line, quote in unquoted field, text after closing quote, backslash escapes, ragged rows) raise `CsvParseError`.
- **Printer** (`format_records`): quotes fields containing `,`/`"`/newline or that are empty, doubling embedded quotes — so `parse(print(doc)) == doc` for every document `parse` can produce.
- **Root façades** `@csv.parse` and `@csv.print` forward to the subpackage, keeping the required root API.

## HPACK (RFC 7541) codec — complete

I implemented the full HPACK codec in MoonBit in the root `hpack` package, filling in every declaration in `hpack_spec.mbt`, and validated it against the RFC and 448 real cross-implementation vectors.

**`moon test` — 163 tests, 163 passed, 0 failed.** `moon check` — 0 errors.

### Implementation (split by responsibility, all files < 200 lines)
- **`integer.mbt`** — prefixed integers (§5.1): minimal encoding; decoding accumulates in `Int64`, rejects values above 2³¹−1 and encodings with more than five continuation octets as `IntegerOverflow`, and ends mid-encoding as `UnexpectedEof`.
- **`string_literal.mbt`** — string literals (§5.2), raw and Huffman.
- **`huffman.mbt` / `huffman_tables.mbt`** — a complete Appendix B coder: MSB-first encoding with ones-padding, and a canonical decoder (per-length consecutive code ranges) that reports `InvalidHuffman` for the EOS symbol, padding longer than 7 bits, and non-ones padding. The 257-symbol tables were generated from the vendored RFC and are Kraft-verified (sum = 1, prefix-free).
- **`static_table.mbt`** — Appendix A, 61 entries.
- **`dynamic_table.mbt`** — exact size accounting (§4.1), newest-first insertion with eviction, the "entry larger than the table" rule, and size-change eviction.
- **`decoder.mbt`** — all five representations (§6), the combined index space, size-update placement/limit rules, and every "MUST be treated as a decoding error" condition.
- **`encoder.mbt`** — the deterministic greedy strategy (exact → indexed with smallest index; name → literal-with-incremental-indexing and insert; else literal name+value and insert), both string-literal forms, the two single-field forms, and `set_max_size` signalling (smallest then final, one update when equal).

### Tests
- **`internals_wbtest.mbt`** — RFC §5.1 examples, every prefix width/boundary, overflow/truncation errors, Huffman vectors and a round trip over all 256 octets, the static table, and dynamic-table behaviour.
- **`rfc_examples_test.mbt`** — Appendix C.2–C.6, with expected wire bytes parsed straight from `specs/rfc7541.txt`; checks **both** directions (encode byte-equality and decode), including C.5/C.6 with a 256-octet table.
- **`decoder_encoder_test.mbt`** — every error variant, size-update placement/limits, cross-block table persistence, and size-update signalling.
- **`compat_corpus_test.mbt`** — 448 real header blocks from the public [hpack-test-case](https://github.com/http2jp/hpack-test-case) corpus (go-hpack, nghttp2, python-hpack, node-http2, haskell-http2 ×3, swift-nio, including the change-table-size and 16384 variants), decoded in sequence and compared to their expected fields.

Together with the supplied property tests (round-trip for both literal forms and "decode never panics"), this covers the general behaviour, not just fixtures.

## Summary

Implemented a complete, general INI parser/printer for the repository's dialect, in the root `ini` package.

### Deliverables
- [scanner.mbt](scanner.mbt) — whitespace/control predicates, clamped range helpers, physical-line splitting (LF/CRLF), and odd/even trailing-backslash continuation joining (recording segment boundaries).
- [value.mbt](value.mbt) — the three value carriers (unquoted, `"…"`, `'…'`), their per-carrier escape tables, inline-comment stripping, and the same-physical-line closing-quote rule.
- [section.mbt](section.mbt) — exact section-header parsing (stray-bracket rejection, trailing-text rejection, `["name"]`/`['name']` quote stripping) and key validation.
- [parser.mbt](parser.mbt) — the `parse` driver: classify blank/comment/section/entry lines, fold into `global` or the current (re-opened) section.
- [printer.mbt](printer.mbt) — `print`, always double-quoting values and re-wrapping section names so `parse(print(doc)) == doc`.
- [ini_edge_test.mbt](ini_edge_test.mbt) — 62 black-box tests derived from `specs/ini.md`.
- [README.md](README.md) — full architecture, algorithm, usage, testing, and design-rationale documentation.

### Key design points
- Works over `Array[Char]` for character-level decisions without surrogate hazards.
- Continuation is decided on the raw line **before** escape processing; a marker removes exactly one backslash and joins directly.
- Quoted values must close on one physical line; join boundaries are tracked so a continuation inside quotes is rejected.
- The first `=`/`:` is the separator; later ones are value text.
- `print` uses double quotes universally, which preserves whitespace/`;`/`#`/separators and escapes the rest, so every value round-trips.

### Validation
- `moon test --deny-warn` → **74/74 pass** (12 provided public incl. both QuickCheck property tests, plus my 62 edge cases).
- `moon check --deny-warn` → 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `moon fmt --check` → clean; `moon info` regenerated `pkg.generated.mbti`.
- Protected files (`ini_spec.mbt`, `ini_qc.mbt`, `specs/`, `*_pub_test.mbt`) are unmodified.

- The provided, unmodifiable files trigger the `implicit_impl_as_method` and `test_unqualified_package` lints; `moon.pkg` disables exactly those two (and moves the test-only `core/test` import to `for "test"`), so the build is warning-free even under `--deny-warn`. ## Key correctness properties

- **Streaming**: every varint/fixed/payload value is reassembled across arbitrarily small `read` calls; `LimitedReader` confines packed decoding to the payload; end-of-stream anywhere inside a value raises.
- **Varints**: any ≤10-byte encoding accepted (non-minimal included), bits beyond the 64th dropped (`80×9 7F` = 2^63), an 11th continuation byte overflows, 32-bit readers take the low 32 bits.
- **Integers**: `int32`/`enum` negatives sign-extend to ten bytes; ZigZag for `sint32/64`; `bool` nonzero ⇒ true.
- **Fixed width** little-endian with bit-exact `float`/`double` (verified signaling-NaN and `-0.0` preservation).
- **Length prefixes** bounded to `0..=2^31-1` (2^32 rejected); payloads gathered in chunks so bogus lengths can't force huge allocations.
- **UTF-8** strict per Unicode table 3-7, keeping all valid scalars including a leading U+FEFF.
- **Keys/groups**: `(field<<3)|wire`, field 0 and wire 6/7 rejected; `read_unknown` skips varint/8/len/4 and recursively skips groups, rejecting mismatched end tags and stray wire 4/6/7.

## Key design points (a real parser, not a lookup table)

- **Splitting**: fragment at the first `#`, query at the first `?`, scheme only when the prefix before `:` matches `ALPHA *(ALPHA/DIGIT/+/-/.)`, authority at a leading `//`, then `[userinfo@]host[:port]`.
- **Validation**: every component checked against its own ABNF character set (controls, space, `<>`, `\`, `^`, backtick, `{}`, `|`, `"`, etc. are rejected everywhere), with `%` accepted only as a two-hex-digit triplet. Path *shape* is enforced (`path-abempty`/`absolute`/`rootless`/`noscheme`), including the no-colon rule for the first `path-noscheme` segment, which also rejects scheme-like-but-invalid inputs like `1http://…`.
- **IP-literals**: IPv6 validated by `::` splitting and group-counting (embedded IPv4 tails count as two), plus RFC 6874 `%25` zone IDs; IPvFuture by its own grammar. Brackets are preserved in `host`.
- **Resolution**: literal Section 5.2.2 strict-mode algorithm and the two-buffer Section 5.2.4 dot-segment routine (`http:g` stays `http:g`).
